title: Hub GCSE History Topic Checklist (Aligned to Edexcel 1HI0)
subtitle: Option 30: Russia and the Soviet Union, 1917–41

exam_structure.overview: Section A tests source inference (4m) and causation (12m). Section B tests historical interpretations and contemporary source utility (36m) plus 4 marks for SPaG.

topics.title: 1. The growth of opposition to the tsar in early 1917
points: Growing discontent among peasants & town workers
Impact of the First World War: military defeats; economic, political & social effects; the Tsar as commander-in-chief

topics.title: 2. The February Revolution
points: Immediate reasons for the February Revolution: e vents in Petrograd in February 1917 (incl. strikes & the mutiny in the army); The Tsar’s absence & abdication

topics.title: 3. The Provisional Government
points: Establishment of the Provisional Government & the problems it faced (incl. ‘Dual Control’ & Soviet Order Number 1); Kerensky
Weaknesses & failures of the Provisional Government
Significance: Kornilov Revolt

topics.title: 4. The Bolshevik Revolution
points: Lenin’s return & activities (incl. the April Theses & the growth in support for the Bolshevik Party); The ‘July Days’
The Bolshevik seizure of power in October 1917; reasons for their success; roles of Trotsky & Lenin

sections.title: Key topic 2: The Bolsheviks in power, 1917–24

topics.title: 1. Early consolidation of power, 1917–18
points: Early Bolshevik decrees of November–December 1917
Removal of opposition (incl. the Constituent Assembly & the execution of Tsar Nicholas II & his family)
Reasons for, main terms & significance of, the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk; Different reactions in Russia to the Treaty

topics.title: 2. The Civil War, 1918–21
points: Reasons for, key events & effects of the Civil War
Reasons for the Bolshevik victory (incl. the strengths of the Bolsheviks, role of Trotsky, foreign intervention & the weaknesses of the Whites)

topics.title: 3. Moves towards totalitarianism
points: The Red Terror & Cheka; The Kronstadt Mutiny
Bolshevik centralisation (incl. Lenin & the Politburo); Setting up of the USSR

topics.title: 4. Economic and social change, 1918–24
points: Reasons for & features of, War Communism; Causes of its unpopularity
Reasons for & features of, the New Economic Policy; Different reactions to the NEP; Its effects on the economy, 1921–24
Social changes (incl. Bolshevik policies on women, education & culture)

sections.title: Key topic 3: Stalin’s rise to power and dictatorship, 1924–41

topics.title: 1. The struggle for power, 1924–28
points: Strengths & weaknesses of Stalin & his rivals (Trotsky, Kamenev, Zinoviev & Bukharin)
Reasons for the emergence of Stalin as leader of the USSR (incl. the removal of rivals for the leadership in the years 1924–28)

topics.title: 2. The use of terror in the 1930s
points: Reasons for, nature of & consequences of the purges (incl. the purges of the armed forces)
Work of the secret police (NKVD); the use of & conditions in, the labour camps
Reasons for & the importance of, the show trials of 1936–1938

topics.title: 3. Propaganda and censorship
points: Official culture, socialist realism, control of education & religion; Media censorship
New Constitution of 1936

topics.title: 4. The Cult of Stalin
points: Meaning of the Cult of Stalin & reasons for its introduction
How the Cult of Stalin was achieved

sections.title: Key topic 4: Economic and social changes, 1924–41

topics.title: 1. Agriculture and collectivisation
points: Stalin’s reasons for changes in agriculture (incl. the problems of the NEP)
Organisation of collectives, mechanisation, widespread opposition & the attack on the kulaks; Famine in Ukraine
Successes & failures of collectivisation

topics.title: 2. Changes in industry
points: Stalin’s motives for rapid industrialisation (incl. the failings of the NEP)
Gosplan, Five-Year Plans & the Stakhanovite Movement
Successes & failures of industrialisation

topics.title: 3. Life in the Soviet Union
points: Living & working conditions in towns & the countryside
Differing experiences of social groups

topics.title: 4. The position of women and ethnic minorities
points: Changes in family life & employment & the political position of women
Reasons for & features of, the persecution of ethnic minorities
